newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rupiah strengthens on liquidity concerns.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rupiah strengthens on liquidity concerns.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah strengthened against the dollar by mid-afternoon on Tuesday on the back of rising liquidity concerns due to the approaching fiscal year-end.
Dealers said offshore players were caught by surprise, triggering broad stop-loss selling and driving the dollar down.
"I think offshore operators do not realise the significance of tax payments due at fiscal year-end," one U.S. bank dealer said, adding that offshore investors were biddish on dollars earlier.
Dealers said local operators' concern on liquidity set the whole market moving following rises of money over tomorrow.
Tom/next swaps rose to 0.35 from 0.2. One-week swaps soared to 2.5/3.0 from 1.3/1.7 points.
The U.S. bank dealer said operators seemed to realise that immediately after completing tax payments, banks have to meet the new reserve requirement rate of five percent in April.
Spot rupiah strengthened to 2,392.00/92.75 at 0730 GMT from 2,395.0/96.0. Tomorrow and today were at 2,391.60/92.25 and 2,394.60/95.10.
One-month swaps increased to 12.00/12.75 from 10.25/11.00, two to 24.0/26.0 from 22.25/23.00, three to 35.5/37.0 from 34.5/36.00 and six to 75.5/76.5 from 74.00/75.00 points.
"It's mainly liquidity-driven. Some economic data released on Tuesday appears to have only minor impact," the U.S. bank dealer said, adding that they were within expectations.
One local bank dealer said operators started to anticipate possible tightening when some state banks swept the money and swap markets, leading to an increase in interbank rates.
"This seem to have alerted the market," he said.
